Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Nexus Energy Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to John Smith, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Nexus Energy Corp.'s Q3 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Tom Reilly, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer, and David Patel, Chief Strategy Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, John, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by:
    1. Progress on strategic initiatives and long-term goals.
    2. Strong customer growth and usage trends.
    3. Favorable comparison of current results to prior periods and guidance.
    4. Effective handling of regulatory lag and mitigation strategies.
    5. Robust forward-looking statements and implications.

Let me provide some more detail on these five key aspects.

First, on progress with our strategic initiatives and long-term goals. We're seeing excellent momentum across our main strategic pillars as we advance our vision to lead as the premier clean energy provider in the Southeast and Mid-Atlantic regions. Our long-term objectives are firmly set around three core commitments: reaching 50% carbon-free generation capacity by 2030, attaining net-zero Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2040, and achieving 8-10% annual EPS growth throughout the decade. This progress is supported by $2.4 billion in capital investments so far this year, aligning perfectly with our $12-14 billion five-year capex plan.

Starting with our accelerated renewables program, which remains our top focus amid rising demand from data centers and electrification. During Q3, we commissioned 450 MW of solar PV across three projects in North Carolina and Georgia—namely Apex Solar Farms I, II, and III. These utility-scale sites feature high-efficiency bifacial panels from First Solar combined with single-axis trackers from Nextracker, delivering a weighted average capacity factor of 28% in their initial quarter, surpassing the regional benchmark of 24%. This elevates our total renewables portfolio to 4.2 GW, accounting for 38% of our 11 GW rate base, improved from 32% last year. We've secured strong PPA interest, with 85% of the new capacity under 15-20 year agreements with hyperscalers such as Google and Microsoft at blended rates of $35/MWh—15% above our traditional gas fleet levels.

Moving forward, we have 1.2 GW of renewables in the pipeline, including 800 MW of community solar in Virginia advancing through PJM's interconnection, taking advantage of IRA tax credit transferability. We've already monetized $450 million in ITC and PTC credits this year via tax equity deals with firms like JPMorgan and BlackRock, enhancing after-tax returns to 12-14% on these projects. In the Southeast, opportunities have emerged from Santee Cooper's coal phase-outs, creating 2 GW of replacement needs, and we're targeting this with our 600 MW Southeast Renewables Hub, aiming for FERC approval next Q2.

Battery energy storage systems are central to our grid modernization efforts, tackling intermittency to support greater renewables integration. We brought online 300 MW/1,200 MWh of BESS at the Charlotte Gateway project using Tesla Megapack 2XL units offering four-hour duration. This site has dispatched 150 GWh year-to-date, generating $25 million from ancillary services in Duke Energy Carolinas' balancing market—40% higher than last year—while avoiding $100 million in transmission and distribution spending through peak load reduction. Our BESS pipeline totals 2.5 GW, with 1 GW in construction, including a 500 MW/2 GWh standalone unit in ERCOT through our joint venture with NextEra Energy Resources. ERCOT's extreme summer peaks from crypto and AI loads highlight the potential, with these projects achieving IRRs over 15% backed by LCIA performance incentives.

We're balancing intermittency with firm clean power. We've filed for a 20-year license renewal on the 1,100 MW Salem Harbor nuclear uprate, incorporating GE Hitachi's BWRX-300 SMR tech for a possible 300 MW addition by 2028—following the industry trend like Constellation Energy's Three Mile Island revival with Microsoft. Nuclear makes up 25% of our dispatchable capacity at a 92% factor, protecting against Henry Hub gas swings that jumped 25% in Q3 due to Freeport LNG issues.

On the customer side, our EV infrastructure rollout has installed 5,000 Level 2 chargers and 200 DC fast chargers in the Carolinas with Electrify America, spurring 22% year-over-year residential load growth to 1.2% via a $50 million heat pump rebate program. Data centers now factor into 15% of our 2030 load forecast, up from 8% in 2022, with 1.5 GW new hyperscaler deals this year. We're partnering with Dominion Energy on the Southeast Reliability Corridor for 500 kV transmission reinforcements to address NERC risks.

Operationally, our $300 million smart grid program is 85% complete, incorporating ABB's Grid eMotion for DER orchestration and Siemens' Spectrum Power for distribution management. This cut SAIDI 18% to 65 minutes and enabled 200 MW VPP from rooftop solar and EVs. In Florida's hurricane zones, microgrid pilots at two substations endured Idalia without outages, beating the state average of four days.

These efforts are delivering financially: renewables and storage added 250 bps to regulated ROE at 10.2%, with development EBITDA at $180 million, up 35%. FCF conversion is 95%, backing our 4.2% dividend yield and $500 million buyback. Challenges like supply chain delays on 100 MW Vestas wind turbines from rare earth shortages and higher rates pressuring 6x net debt-to-EBITDA persist, but our $1.8 billion liquidity and green bond access at 150 bps spreads keep us secure. Regulatory support is strong: FERC Order 2023 speeds PJM projects, and state IRPs in Georgia and North Carolina back our 70/20/10 clean mix by 2035.

In short, we're on track with our roadmap, shifting to 60% renewables plus storage by 2030 while upholding stability. This sets us to seize the $100 billion Southeast clean energy market for top TSR against peers like Southern Company or Entergy.

Second, regarding customer growth and usage trends across residential, commercial, and industrial classes. This quarter highlights the powerful demand drivers in utilities from electrification, data center expansion, and industrial reshoring, as we push forward with grid hardening and capacity additions.

In total, customer numbers rose 2.8% year-over-year to 4.2 million, with weather-normalized retail sales up 3.6% to 28.4 million MWh—the best quarterly load growth since Q1 2022, exceeding the U.S. EIA average of 2.1%. Our Southeast areas led with 4.2% growth from Florida and Georgia population shifts, while Midwest ops grew 2.9% on manufacturing returns.

Residential customers climbed 2.5% to 3.1 million, driven by household formation and migration. Usage increased 1.8% normalized to 15.2 million MWh, topping our full-year midpoint of 1.5%. Electrification is key: EV penetration reached 12% from 8%, aided by our EV managed charging with ChargePoint and Tesla VPP. Heat pump users show 15-20% higher evening peaks, boosted by IRA Section 25C. We've implemented TOU rates for 1.2 million via 95% AMI completion, shifting 8% off-peak and lifting load factor to 61% from 58%. In Florida post-hurricanes, solar-plus-storage grew 22%, handling 45,000 DERs via our AI-powered Gridworks platform.

Commercial customers edged up 1.2% to 850,000, but usage jumped 3.4% to 8.1 million MWh—our strongest area. Hybrid work steadied office vacancies at 18-20% in Atlanta and Charlotte, while retail/hospitality rebounded 5%. Supermarkets and cold storage grew 12% on supply chain shifts. Notably, small data centers and edge computing added 15 new hyperscaler leases for 500 MW in Georgia, raising peak demand 4.7 GWh/day. We've countered with 250 MW demand response via Enel X and microgrids at 200 sites to ease 18-month queues.

Industrial customers surged 4.1% to 50,000, with usage soaring 7.2% to 5.1 million MWh. Data centers dominate: Google Cloud and AWS added 1.2 GW to our queue, 15% of 2025-2028 capacity. AI racks hit 100+ kW densities, double 2022, as crypto miners stabilize at 5% load. Reshoring shines: automotive batteries like our Tennessee gigafactory offtake added 300 GWh up 25%, with CHIPS/IRA 45X credits; Midwest steel/chemicals up 6% on electrification. Peak demand reached 4.8 GW, up 9%, driving $1.2 billion in three 500 kV lines with PJM/MISO.

These patterns validate our 4-6% CAGR load growth to 2030, beating EEI peers' 2.5-3.5%. We've de-risked 80% of queue with 2 GW renewables-storage hybrids via Apex Renewables by 2026. FERC 2023 aids, plus 500 MW residential battery VPPs lift EBITDA 50 bps. Southeast industrial leads Northeast residential 2x, so 60% capex there. Full-year guide: 3.2% load growth, EPS $4.85-$5.05.

Third, on the comparison of our current period results to prior periods and guidance. Let's review our Q3 financials ended September 30, 2024, against last year and Q2, plus year-to-date, with updated outlook. Results are GAAP, non-GAAP in release and 10-Q.

Q3 revenues hit $2.82 billion, up 7.7% from $2.62 billion in Q3 2023 and 4.2% from Q2's $2.71 billion. Adjusted EBITDA was $952 million, rising 8.2% YoY from $880 million and 3.8% sequentially from $917 million. Diluted EPS reached $1.25 versus $1.10 prior year and $1.18 Q2. YTD revenues totaled $8.15 billion, up 6.9% from $7.63 billion; EBITDA $2.71 billion, +9.1%; EPS $3.42 vs. $3.05.

This stems from industry tailwinds like data center/AI demand and electrification, tempered by milder weather. Regulated utilities (65% portfolio) led growth; competitive gen and renewables gained from ERCOT/PJM merchant prices.

Regulated utilities revenues rose 9.1% YoY to $1.85 billion across MISO/SERC. kWh sales up 5.2% to 28.2 million MWh on 12% C&I surge from Microsoft/Google PPAs. Residential flat with 8% fewer CDDs. $1.2 billion 2023 capex including 400 MW Ohio BESS lifted ROE 200 bps to 10.4% in Indiana settlement. Sequentially, +5.3% on summer peaks and full-quarter 250 MW Georgia solar-storage at 28% factor.

Competitive generation revenues up 12.4% to $685 million from $610 million. ERCOT hedge $45/MWh vs. $38; spark spreads $32/MWh. Liberty Peaker 1,200 MW at 62% factor vs. 55%. 15% unhedged added $45 million margin.

Renewables/storage revenues $285 million, +18%, 3.8 million MWh from 4,500 MW portfolio at 32% factors via AI curtailment cuts 15% at Rattlesnake Solar. IRA PTC/ITC upped yields 25%.

Generation totaled 42.6 million MWh, +6.8%; renewables 22% vs. 18%. Thermal outages 2.1% vs. EIA 3.5% peer via GE 7HA digital twins.

Fuel up 10% to $420 million at $3.85/MMBtu, 85% hedged $3.20. O&M +4% to $510 million on labor, offset 8% automation/drone savings. D&A +7% $380 million new assets; interest steady $210 million at 4.2% debt cost.

Op cash $1.05 billion +11%, funding $450 million dividends, $300 million growth capex. Liquidity $4.2 billion, net debt/EBITDA 3.4x vs. 4.0x target.

By ISO: ERCOT +15% dispatch on heat; PJM flat but $25 million BESS freq reg; CAISO $15 million wildfire costs offset by microgrids; Midwest +3% reshoring.

This reinforces "Reliable Renewables": retire 1,200 MW coal 2025, repower 900 MW peakers/600 MW storage. 1.2 GW new PPAs at 10-12% IRR; Illinois green H2 pilot 5% blend, 20% NOx cut. $500 million M&A dry powder for storage.

Raised FY2024 guide: revenues $10.9-11.1B (prior $10.8-11.0B); EBITDA $3.65-3.75B (prior $3.60-3.70B); EPS $4.55-4.65 (prior $4.50-4.60); capex $2.4B, 55% growth. Assumes normal weather, $3.50 gas, no disallowances. Upside: 20%+ data center growth, FERC 2222 DERs.

For 2025, 6-8% rate base to $28B, 7-9% EPS compound, 5% dividend to $2.40/share. Formal guide February.

Fourth, addressing regulatory lag and our mitigation strategies—a persistent industry issue intensified by clean energy shifts and inflation. Regulatory lag is the delay between incurring capex and O&M—like grid hardening, renewables expansion, nuclear uprates—and rate recovery via PUCs. This squeezes ROE, especially with high rates where AFUDC falls short on equity costs.

For Nexus Energy Corp., aggregate lag was about $285 million at June 30 across Northeast and Midwest—NY, PA, IL, OH—up 12% YoY, a 180 bps ROE drag, pulling regulated from 10.2% target to 9.1% H1. PJM hit hardest at $140 million from $1.2B deferred transmission under FERC Order 1000 post-Vista. MISO milder $95 million thanks to formula rates, but pressured by Illinois CEJA.

NY NYSPSC slowest: Brooklyn-Queens 316 MW battery like NextEra Manatee cost $450 million CWIP, 18-month lag cost $22 million AFUDC at 7.5% proxy. PA PUC friendlier, recouping 65% Susquehanna nuclear uprate lag in nine months.

Mitigations target <$150 million lag by 2026 for earnings resilience. Primarily proactive ratemaking: four cases/settlements last 18 months for $420 million revenue, 75% CWIP vs. historical 55%. Pending Ohio PUCO MYRP with quarterly true-ups like Eversource MA could recover $180 million for 800 MW solar-storage.

Second, riders/trackers cover 45% cost of service from 32% 2021. Fuel/power trackers saved $65 million gas volatility post-Ukraine/Freeport. Renewables rider like Duke NC sped 1.2 GW IRA projects: Buckeye Wind 400 MW First Solar bifacials, Illinois batteries. PA decoupling covers 85% distribution from EV/heat pump throughput drops.

Third, source reduction via self-supply/hedging: 2024 PJM capacity $240/MW-day, 15% above clear, +$45 million wholesale YTD. $150 million grid mod with Siemens/Schneider AMI 2.0/DERMS for dynamic ratings deferring $300 million capex. NY VPPs aggregate 50 MW residential batteries for NYISO ancillaries at 10-12% IRR uplift non-ratebase.

Advocacy via EEI/commissions: FERC Order 1920 ROE incentives, state ESG ratchets +50 bps for RPS/decarb. 80/20 clean capex $8B to 2028, 40% storage/H2 peakers; IRA PTC/ITC transfers $120 million cash.

Lag peaks 2025 on $2.5B PJM RTEP, but strategies yield 200-250 bps ROE by 2027. IRP stress-tested at 5% inflation/50 bps hikes, on pace 6-8% EPS growth.

Fifth, on forward-looking statements and their implications. Our comments today, including Q&A, include forward-looking statements under the 1995 Reform Act safe harbor. Based on current expectations on economy, regs, commodities, loads, markets—actuals may vary per SEC risks like 2024 ERCOT Polar Vortex, Henry Hub gas, FERC delays, RPS changes. No update obligation.

For Nexus, FY2025 adjusted EPS $4.65-4.95, 7-12% over 2024 $4.35 midpoint. Assumes normal weather HDD/CDD 10-year avg, $12B five-year capex. Revenues 9-11% to $8.2-8.5B on regulated rate base Northeast and PJM/ERCOT merchant.

Load: 4-6% CAGR to 2030 vs. 2.5% hist, from data centers/AI. PJM 15 GW gas/nuclear/renewables secured 1.2 GW PPAs Microsoft/Google $65/MWh CPI-escalate. ERCOT 20% merchant 2.5 GW peakers 85% factor 2024 heat at $250/MWh scarcity 15% runtime. Data centers add 50 TWh U.S. by 2028 EIA, backing 10-12% ROE, premium to 18x utility P/E.

Clean transition: $4.5B renewables/storage to 2027. 1.8 GW Southwest solar First Solar 25.5% ratios; 800 MW Midwest Vestas wind. 500 MW BESS Tesla 4-hr arb CAISO duck curve 20% spreads 15% IRR. 300 MW offshore Atlantic Ørsted FID H2 2025 BOEM, $50-55/MWh IRA PTC.

Nuclear: NRC Palisades 1,100 MW restart Q4 2026 $1.5B DOE like Constellation. Two 77 MW NuScale SMR Michigan MISO 2028. Carbon-free to 60% 2030 from 45%, IRA 45U $15/MWh ZEP.

Capex 2025 $3.4-3.6B: 55% renew/storage, 25% transmission reconductor 500 mi 345 kV NERC, 20% nuclear/mod. 60/40 debt/equity A- profile 4.75% 10-yr notes Q1. Tax 18% post-IRA, FCF $1.8B, 6% div growth $2.42/share, $500M buybacks.

Northeast 40% earnings NY REV/MA Clean Peak, rate base +8% $18B. PJM 2028/29 auctions $120-140/kW-yr +15%. ERCOT hedge 70% gas $3-4.50 collars. CA SB100 gas retire but CCUS Exxon 90% CO2 $30/ton.

Positions for high-single EPS growth > Dominion/NextEra 6-8%. 2.5 GW SPP/MISO queue top decile organic. Risks interconnection 5-yr LBNL, steel tariffs; $2B liquidity/hedges mitigate. Implies 12-15% TSR: 6% yield +6% div + apprec $1T electrification.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Tom Reilly to discuss the financials.

Tom Reilly: Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. For the Q3, we reported earnings per share of $1.25 and revenue of $2.82 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $600 million, primarily focused on renewables integration and grid modernization. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders. We anticipate 7-9% EPS growth in the coming years.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Tom. Let me provide an update on the operational front. We are seeing improved efficiency in our gas-fired power plants due to the implementation of digital twin predictive maintenance technology. This has resulted in a 15% increase in output.

David Patel: Thank you, Lisa. Turning to our long-term strategy, we are actively exploring opportunities in the battery energy storage and green hydrogen space. We believe this will be a key driver of future growth.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Tom, Lisa, and David. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for data center load integration?

Sarah Thompson: Certainly. As we highlighted, data centers are a major growth driver, representing 15% of our load forecast through 2030. We've secured 1.2 GW in new PPAs with hyperscalers and are investing in transmission and storage to manage peaks, with 80% of our queue de-risked through co-located renewables and batteries.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: What is your outlook for regulatory lag going forward?

Tom Reilly: Our strategies are on track to reduce lag below $150 million by 2026 through proactive rate cases, riders covering 45% of costs, and operational efficiencies like VPPs. We expect ROE expansion of 200-250 bps by 2027 despite peak pressures in 2025.

Operator: Our next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel: How are you mitigating risks related to commodity price volatility and weather?

Lisa Chen: We're hedging 85% of gas exposure and maintaining best-in-class outage rates at 2.1%. Grid resilience investments, including smart grid and microgrids, have proven effective, as seen in zero outages during recent hurricanes versus state averages.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the Q3, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Nexus Energy Corp. for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Nexus Energy Corp.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
